source.title: How unrealistic optimism is maintained in the face of reality

confidence_rationale: Canonical, high-venue, neurally-grounded demonstration of exactly the asymmetry SD-076 posits (desirable errors incorporated, undesirable errors under-coded). Confidence held below 0.8 because the domain is self-referential beliefs about future life events, not a running estimate of one's own predictive accuracy, and because the paradigm's statistical basis was subsequently contested (see the Ni 2023 and Garrett 2018 entries in this directory).
failure_signatures: The asymmetry is carried by a FAILURE TO CODE undesirable errors, not by a symmetric rate difference -- if REE implements SD-076 as a pure two-rate EMA it reproduces the outcome but not the mechanism, and will not show the selective error-tracking dropout this paper measures.

Optimistic individuals showed reduced error tracking in right inferior prefrontal gyrus specifically for negative updates -- a between-subject trait axis SD-076's single global asymmetry parameter cannot express.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Participants updated beliefs about the likelihood of future life events more in response to better-than-expected information than to worse-than-expected information, and this selectivity was mediated by a relative failure to neurally code estimation errors calling for a pessimistic update.
mapping.ree_translation: REE reads this as the biological warrant for SD-076's asymmetric precision EMA: the E3 selector's running-variance estimate should incorporate evidence of good self-accuracy faster than evidence of bad self-accuracy, so rv drifts below the true error mean across a waking episode -- supplying the daytime precision drift that MECH-204's sleep recalibration presupposes.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper measures updating of beliefs ABOUT THE WORLD (probability of future life events), not updating of a SELF-ACCURACY / precision estimate. SD-076 is a claim about the second-order quantity. The transfer assumes the same valence asymmetry applies when the thing being estimated is one's own predictive error, which this paper does not test. It is also a human self-report paradigm with no analogue of REE's per-step prediction error.
mapping.source_context: Healthy adult humans, fMRI, self-referential probability estimation for ~80 adverse life events with feedback on population base rates.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high (Nature Neuroscience, neural + behavioural convergence) but discounted slightly by the post-2016 replication dispute. Mapping fidelity is the binding constraint: first-order world beliefs vs second-order precision. Transfer risk moderate-high -- human episodic self-belief to an agent's running variance estimate is a long jump.
